title: Scheduled RBAC-aware streaming export for audit console with anomaly sampling
creator: Ava Chen
description: Add a scheduled export capability to the Audit Console that streams large result sets incrementally to CSV/JSON destinations while enforcing RBAC v2 redaction rules and optional anomaly sampling. This ticket covers the backend streaming API, a background scheduler for recurring saved queries, role-aware field masking, and a lightweight console UI for creating and managing scheduled exports. The goal is to support exports that can run over large time ranges without blocking the UI or overloading the runtime, to allow security teams to receive periodic dumps, and to enable on-demand ad-hoc streaming exports for investigative workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Console: user can create a scheduled export from a saved query with cadence (daily/weekly/monthly) and destination (S3 pre-signed URL or in-console download)
API: provide a cursor-based streaming endpoint that returns NDJSON chunks and a durable export job record for large queries
RBAC: exported rows and fields respect RBAC v2 policies; sensitive fields are redacted or masked per role rules
Formats: exports available as CSV, JSON (array), and NDJSON; JSON export does not exceed memory limits for large result sets
Resilience: scheduled exports run in background workers with retries, idempotency, and backoff; failures surface to the Jobs dashboard and via notification hooks
Anomaly sampling: optional sampling flag that includes a prioritized subset of events flagged by the anomaly detector for faster triage
Security: exports written to temporary encrypted storage with KMS-backed keys and are accessible only to users/roles with export permission
Observability: per-export metrics (row count, duration, bytes), and a console job view with logs and retry history
tech_notes: Use cursor-based pagination (cursor token opaque to client) to stream results from the audit events store; worker resumes from last committed cursor on retry
Implement a streaming writer that flushes NDJSON/CSV chunks to temporary S3 (or internal blob store) to avoid high memory usage
Apply RBAC v2 policy evaluation at the row and field level during streaming to avoid post-processing leaks; redact values using deterministic masking for reproducibility
Support two export modes: ad-hoc immediate streaming (user waits for download link) and scheduled background job (email/console notification with link)
Add index hints to the audit store query planner for time-range heavy exports to reduce scan cost; consider partition pruning by event_date
Anomaly sampling hooks: consult the anomaly-score pipeline; pull top-K anomalies first then stream remainder if requested
Include an export manifest with job metadata, applied filters, policy version, and redaction schema to aid auditability
Use job-level encryption keys rotated via KMS and short-lived pre-signed URLs for user downloads; auto-expire artifacts after retention window
tasks: Design API contract for streaming exports (GET /v1/audit/exports/stream?cursor=...) and POST /v1/audit/exports to create jobs
Backend: implement ExportJob model, worker queue, and cursor checkpointing
Backend: implement RBAC-aware row/field redaction library and integrate with export pipeline
Storage: implement temporary encrypted storage with auto-expire and S3 integration for large exports
UX: add "Create scheduled export" flow to Saved Queries with cadence and destination options
UX: Jobs dashboard entry showing recent export jobs, status, metrics, and download links
E2E: build test harness for large export runs, including simulated failures and resume tests
Docs: document export formats, retention policy, and admin controls for export permission

decisions: Prefer cursor-based resume over page-based offsets to avoid duplicate/missing rows during concurrent writes
Redaction performed at export time (read-time) to ensure up-to-date RBAC semantics; store export manifest referencing policy version
Use NDJSON as the canonical streaming format; CSV/JSON derived from NDJSON output for user convenience
risks: Large exports can stress the audit store if queries are unbounded; mitigation: impose default time range limits and advise pagination
Mistakes in RBAC evaluation could leak sensitive fields; mitigation: unit tests + policy-versioned manifests + security review
Retention and cleanup bugs could leave sensitive artifacts accessible; mitigation: auto-expire, audit of cleanup jobs, and monitoring
rollout_plan: alpha: internal-only scheduled exports for Security Ops team with short retention (48h)
beta: gated opt-in for customers with Admin role and export permission; monitor job metrics and S3 costs
GA: enable UI by default for org-admins once performance and security sign-offs complete
tests: Unit: RBAC redaction library coverage for all sensitive fields and role permutations
Integration: simulated long-running export with forced worker restart to validate resume semantics
Perf: end-to-end throughput tests for CSV/NDJSON export across representative row sizes
Security: automated privacy smoke tests that scan exported artifacts for raw PII
audit_fields_masking: user_email: masked to user****@example.com except for org-admins
request_body: redacted for fields marked 'sensitive' in schema
retention_considerations: Temporary export artifacts expire after configurable window (default 7 days). Admins may extend for compliance but must opt into longer retention with audit logging of retention changes. Exports are encrypted with KMS; access to export download links requires export_job.read permission.
